newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil federal court rules in favor of wage hike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil federal court rules in favor of wage hike.

text.p: A federal court in Rio de Janeiro has followed a precedent set by Brazil's highest court and granted 12,350 workers at the city's federal university a 28.9 percent wage hike, a court spokesman said on Friday.

The decision was based on a ruling by the Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) last month in favor of 11 civil servants who claimed they were entitled to a 28.9 percent pay rise awarded to the armed forces in 1993, the spokesman said.
The February STF ruling set a precedent for other courts to grant a similar wage hike to other public sector workers.
Earlier this week, 10,000 employees of the social security services won a similar case in a Brasilia court.

If extended to the entire public sector workforce of one million current and retired civil servants, the pay rises could cost the government an additional $5 billion a year in payroll and $20 billion in backdated pay.
The court spokesman said the university management could appeal against the court decision, in which case the STF has the final word.
